left.subheading: Building accessible GOV.UK Design System components in React.

paragraphs: Most GOV.UK services are built with Nunjucks, but a growing number run on React — and govuk-frontend's official package isn't written for that world. The CSS and JS ship as-is, so getting an accessible, spec-accurate component working in a React app means writing the JSX by hand and being deliberate about how you hand DOM control over to a library that expects to own it.

This project walks through three components built this way: an Accordion that wires up govuk-frontend's JS without fighting React's rendering for control of the DOM, a Character count that debounces its live limit announcement so screen readers aren't spammed on every keystroke, and Tabs using the same progressive-enhancement pattern. Along the way I hit a classic SSR gotcha in Next.js, where govuk-frontend's component classes reference HTMLElement as a static class field evaluated the instant the module loads, crashing the server render. I fixed it with a client-only component that dynamically imports govuk-frontend inside useEffect and calls initAll() once per page.

accordionItems.title: What is GOV.UK Frontend?
accordionItems.content: GOV.UK Frontend provides styles, JavaScript and assets for building services that follow the GOV.UK Design System.

accordionItems.title: How does the accordion work?
accordionItems.content: The GOV.UK Frontend JavaScript progressively enhances the accordion markup with the interactive behaviour.

accordionItems.title: Can I have multiple sections open?
accordionItems.content: Yes. GOV.UK accordions allow multiple sections to be open at the same time.
